target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D122) covers customer concentrations, stating no single customer exceeded 10% in 2023, while citing historical concentrations for Kingston (12% in 2022) and WPG (11% in 2022/13%). The 2024 filings split this topic: D121 introduces the segment revenue table (contextual, but part of the concentration discussion structure); D122 states the current 2024 status (one customer at 10%) and reiterates the 2023 status (no customer >=10%); D123 provides the historical 2022 context (12% and 11% customers) which directly corresponds to the Kingston and WPG data in the 2023 record. These three 2024 disclosures collectively cover the same specific subject matter of customer revenue concentration thresholds and historical comparisons as the 2023 record.

comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO disclose significant single-customer concentration affecting both revenue and receivables, though the magnitude differs. comparisons.comparison: INTC discusses customer concentration in Item 8 but focuses on the composition of revenue from its largest customers rather than disclosing specific percentage thresholds of total revenue like MU. While MU explicitly states that one customer accounted for 10% of total revenue, INTC's disclosure is qualitative, stating that 'substantially all' revenue from its three largest customers originated from specific operating segments. This indicates a focus on business segment dependency rather than a specific single-customer revenue threshold risk comparable to MU's quantitative disclosure.
